7F8387.name: Stripe image record 2 data (tile)
7F8387.kind: byte/word in the stripe image buffer, indexed by buffer offset (X)
desc: Part of the VRAM stripe image buffer that starts at $7F837D ($7F837B holds the current write index).
X is the buffer index of the record being built, so this is a fixed offset ($0A) into it, not a variable.
Break bridge stores $38FC here (blank tile $FC, attributes $38) as the data of its second record.
The Map16 page 1 / wings and event-tile routines write the second record's length word at this offset.

7F8389.name: Stripe image end marker (record 2)
7F8389.kind: byte/word in the stripe image buffer, indexed by buffer offset (X)
desc: Offset in the stripe image buffer ($7F837D+X) where the two-record writers place the terminator.
Break bridge stores $00FF, i.e. end-of-stripe marker $FF, right after the second record.
The Map16 page 1 / wings routine and the event-tile routines write their own record data or
marker at this same offset. The NMI stripe uploader stops when it reads $FF as a record header.

7F838B.name: Stripe image record 3 data
7F838B.kind: byte/word in the stripe image buffer, indexed by buffer offset (X)
desc: Offset $0E into the stripe image buffer ($7F837D+X). Written by the event-tile and Map16 page 1 / wings
routines as part of the record they build; never read back, the NMI stripe uploader consumes it.
Exact contents depend on the routine's record layout.

7F838D.name: Stripe image end marker (late)
7F838D.kind: byte in the stripe image buffer, indexed by buffer offset (X)
desc: Stripe image terminator. The Map16 page 1 / wings routine and the event-tile 2x2 draw routine
store $FF here after their two records so the NMI stripe uploader knows where the batch ends.
Written only; X is the buffer index taken from $7F837B.

7F83AF.name: Level end tally time digits
7F83AF.kind: byte table in the stripe image buffer, indexed by offset (X)
desc: Tile slots of the third text row of the level end tally, in the stripe image buffer ($7F837B index + $34).
The tally routine copies the time digits [$0F31+Y] into it, two bytes apart (tile, then attribute),
then replaces leading zero digits with blank tile $FC so the time is not zero-padded.
Read back once per digit for that leading-zero test.

7FC800.name: Map16 tile high byte table
7FC800.kind: byte table (X = Map16 tile/block offset); high-byte companion of $7EC800
desc: Second half of the level or overworld tile map: the high byte of each entry, with the low byte at
$7EC800+X. Used for Map16 tile numbers and for the overworld tile layout.
Cleared or initialised by the level buffer fill routine (Map16 tile pointers), set to 0 for a
broken bridge tile, written by the boss room tile and overworld setup routines, and read by the
layer 1 map page draw routine when it builds the tilemap buffer.
Values: 0 = high byte zero for the tile.
